name: Liuwei Dihuang pill
short: Diabetic kidney disease trials (pills or decoction): adverse events 4.2% vs 4.3%, mostly mild to moderate. Lupus nephritis and cognitive add-on trials: fewer than control. Safety reporting incomplete.
text: A 2026 meta-analysis of 11 randomized trials (1007 patients) of Liuwei Dihuang pills or decoction added to conventional treatment for early diabetic kidney disease found that only 6 trials reported adverse events: 12 of 287 (4.2%) in the Liuwei Dihuang groups and 12 of 277 (4.3%) in the control groups, with no significant difference and most events mild to moderate; the authors said incomplete safety reporting limits this finding. In a randomized trial in 64 people with lupus nephritis, all treated with prednisone and intravenous cyclophosphamide, the group also given Liuwei Dihuang pill had a significantly lower incidence of adverse reactions; the abstract does not give the numbers or describe the reactions. A 2026 meta-analysis of 12 randomized trials (1137 participants) in cognitive disorders reported fewer adverse events with Liuwei Dihuang added to conventional treatment (the abstract does not say whether as pills or decoction), although reporting quality was limited. The abstracts do not list the herbs in the formula. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
